about: Per-map strategy hints from community guides (wiki strategy sections, guide-video descriptions, Steam/web guides, BTD6 Index records); the plain-language findings and every source are in docs/map_strategies.md. Edit by hand and run tests/test_map_hints_offline.py, which checks that every spot is legal for its tower on the map's geometry, in build order (each spot given the towers before it), for the longest game its build serves.
coords: at = [fx, fy]: fractions of the 1920x1200 game window (x from the left, y from the top), the same frame as MapModel.cell_to_frac / mapgeom.Projection.to_frac.

fields.insight: why a naive plan loses on this map and what players do instead
fields.lane_type: single | simultaneous (several lanes every round) | alternating (lanes take turns by round) | rotating (spawn sides change by round) | merging (several entrances, one exit)
fields.builds: spot lists in buy order, each for the modes listed; 'default': true serves every mode no other build of the map claims. towers = the build's tower kinds (preferred towers for those modes); hero = the guide's hero; last_round = the game length the spots were checked for
fields.spots: tower (a towers.TOWERS kind or 'hero' with 'hero': id), at, note (its job in the build), where (the spot in words)
fields.avoid: towers that do not work on this map as main damage, why, and optionally only in 'modes'
fields.removables: obstacles worth buying (names from mapgeom.removables), when and why; buy: recommended | optional | never
fields.mechanics_data: machine-readable map rules (pane cycle, prime rounds, melt rounds, ...)
fields.model_gaps: places the guides use that the bot's map model gets wrong (to check in game)

Luminous Cove.insight: Two lanes alternate by round and both loop round the heart-shaped pond in the middle; the only land is the strip along the bottom, and every land spot reaches one lane only. A land plan therefore defends every other round (lost at round 49). Build in the heart pond (subs, a buccaneer going to Carrier Flagship, Admiral Brickell) and add snipers on the bottom-left land, which see about 70% of both lanes.
Luminous Cove.lanes: odd rounds: top-left entrance, clockwise round the heart pond, exit bottom-right; even rounds: top-right entrance, anticlockwise, exit bottom-left

Covered Garden.insight: Glass panes cover three of the four garden quarters and the open quarter moves clockwise every round, so a tower under the glass can only be placed or upgraded one round in four. The bot treats pane ground as closed and ran out of spots (lost at round 76 with $49,876 unspent). Build on the always-open strip left of the garden with global towers (heli, ace, sniper) and their supports; the top-left quarter is the best pane ground once the bot can time it.

Ancient Portal.insight: One entrance spirals clockwise into a portal; bloons leave through the right lane unless the free 'Realign Portal' device at the bottom centre is clicked (the bot never clicks it). A lone Spike Factory by the exit sees under 40% of the right lane and none of the spiral (Deflation lost at round 54). Put ninjas and an alchemist on the land strip inside the spiral, the hero on the pedestal below it (+1 damage, +30% range for heroes) and boats/subs in the pond.
Ancient Portal.lanes: spiral from the top into the portal, then the right lane (default) or the walled left lane (only after clicking the realign device)

Bloonarius Prime.insight: On prime-numbered rounds bloons drop into a swamp hole by the entrance and take the short right lane; every other round uses the long left lane. No land spot covers both lanes well, so a Spike Factory at one exit cannot hold the map (Deflation lost at round 49). Use global towers (aces, heli, snipers with sight of both lanes) or one defence per lane.

No ground spot lets a short-range tower hit both lanes, so one cluster leaks the other lane (lost at round 46). Build mirrored pairs (one per lane, in the right-hand corners) and lean on global towers: four snipers in the courtyard quarters, an ace on the raised central platform.

Last Resort.insight: Bloons always enter along the top edge, then take one of four loops in a 4-round cycle (big, medium, small, straight), each faster than the last; only the top lane is used every round. Short-range towers on the right block or inside the big loop miss the small-loop and straight rounds (lost at round 24, 64 lives on the small-loop round). Use snipers from the inner strip of the big loop (they see ~75% of the top lane), a Pursuit heli, and a Perma-Spike as far right as possible; the $1,000 frozen pool opens the best spot on the map for a sub or boat.
Last Resort.lanes: round mod 4 = 1 big loop (+80% speed), 2 medium (+40%), 3 small (+25%), 0 straight along the top (+15%); all share the top lane and exit top-right

Players pack short-range towers at the right junction plus a boat in the water next to it. The bot's boomerang/tack build had no MOAB damage at round 40: by then the junction needs Ninja 4-0-2 + alchemist and a 0-4-2 boat.
Pat's Pond.lanes: top lane enters left and exits right; bottom lane enters right and exits left (the BAD uses the top lane, exiting right)

Enchanted Glade.insight: Two lanes alternate (odd rounds bottom-left, even rounds top-right) but share the wavy stretch below the centre and the final climb into the cherry-tree exit. The bottom-centre island right under that stretch is the best ground on the map. Round 63 (122 ceramics + 75 leads, odd = bottom-left lane) needs crowd damage there: Ninja 4-0-2 + alchemist and a Glue Bloon Solver (5-2-0) by round 62. The bot lost all lives inside round 63 with its spike factories on an island that sees no track and ninjas on the wrong path.
Enchanted Glade.lanes: odd rounds enter bottom-left, even rounds top-right; both end going up into the exit at (0.43,0.39)
